answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake in a shared kernel contract before it may attest work: creating ten fake agents costs ten stakes, and slashing burns the stake of any identity caught attesting fraud. One bad attestation then sends a ripple through the attacker's own capital, while honest agents need only a whisper of reputation history to keep participating — forging many identities scales the cost linearly, but the reward for cheating stays flat.
